_help: THIS FILE CONTROLS THE WHOLE SITE: the order, the sections and how cards look.
ORDER: sections show top to bottom in the order below; projects show in the order of each section's "projects" list. Move a slug up or down to reorder.
MOVE A PROJECT: cut its slug from one section's list and paste it into another.
NEW SECTION: copy a section block and give it a new id (lowercase-with-dashes), title, note and list of slugs.
Any project not listed in a section still shows, in a section called More at the end.
settings.homeLayout: "sections" (grouped, with the outline) or "strip" (one sideways strip, same order).
settings.outline: true shows the contents list at the top of the home page; false hides it.
settings.cardsPerRow: 2, 3 or 4 on desktop (phones always show 1).
settings.showKind: true shows each project's kind under its name on the cards.

Per project, optional: "featured": true makes the card twice as wide; "hidden": true takes it off the home page and out of Next project (its page still works by direct link); "status": "In progress" adds a small tag.
ADDING A PROJECT: add a block to "projects", put its slug in a section, add media/<slug>.mp4 + .jpg and covers/<slug>-wide.jpg, and add the slug to the rewrites in vercel.json.
Analytics links are private and never go in this file.

projects.name: Edge Lab
projects.title: edge lab
projects.why: When getting to a higher level of anything, you cannot simply rely on talent and gut feeling to retain the excellency you had before. Not when everyone competing for the position is on your level or better, this is a way to stand out in a standardised test format. When everyone has played the game before where does your edge come from?
projects.what: Interactive games for trading-interview prep: market making, ETF arbitrage, Bayes, Kelly sizing and a poker room, plus a Daily Gauntlet with a leaderboard.

projects.name: Root T
projects.title: root t
projects.why: The Black-Schoels formula (BS) is one of the most intimidating formulas I have ever had the mind-cluttering pleasure to lay eyes on, in a struggle to break down and model it with comparison to the Monte-Carlo (MS) system on a European call option this was the result.
projects.what: Prices a European call option with 100,000 random simulations, then compares the result live against the Black-Scholes formula across 40 strikes and 20 maturities.

projects.name: The Irrational Margin
projects.title: the irrational margin
projects.why: After learning about the assumptions within economics regarding “rationality” my interest piqued. Why did economists assume normal civillians make perfect decisions when it rarely happens? To enquire further into this and personally document my findings I developed this blog.
projects.what: A blog of essays on behavioural economics, where psychology meets the way people spend, save and choose.

projects.name: The Healing Pages
projects.title: the healing pages
projects.why: As a neurodivergent individual, the expression of emotions and rash decision making has lead to undesireable outcomes in the past, not saying that I wish to never make a mistake again I want to journal the mistakes I have made, the thoughts I had before. It also is something to do late at night to “wrap the night up” and signal to myself it's time to go to sleep.
projects.what: A daily journal that tracks your streak, pages and word count, shows a calendar of what you've written, and has a recite mode for reading a page out loud.

projects.name: IB AA HL Lab
projects.title: ib aa hl lab
projects.why: I wanted to revise IB Maths AA probability properly, and give other students on the course something better than a page of formulas. Mainly it's formatted towards my way of learning one of the most annoying and knowledge based topics in AAHL, unlike calculus where the application of formulas will get the answer. It started as a probability-only site; I've since been adding the rest of the course one unit at a time, starting with the ones I find hardest, and renamed it once it outgrew probability.
projects.what: Units on Probability, Vectors, Differential Equations and Proof, each with live models you can drag, exam-style worked examples with mark schemes, Casio fx-CG50 and TI-84 keystrokes, and unlimited randomised practice questions with full working.

projects.name: Study Tracker
projects.title: study tracker
projects.why: Personally, studying has always been a matter of discipline, making myself sit at a desk to review and memorise items. To make it both easier to get started with and be consistent I built a tracker that natively on my computer allows me to keep track of everything.
projects.what: Allows students to have a hub where everything study related combined into one spot, to ease the pain of studying.

projects.name: Mahjong Crash Course
projects.title: mahjong crash course
projects.why: Since bouncing around major cities from Sichuan and Shenzhen to Sydney then to Shanghai (I don't know why my family seems to love cities with names starting with S) I've always struggled to connect with my Chinese heritage after being in Australia for 12 years. I built this as a way to combat that, to align myself in something I am very proud of which is my family and our traditions.
projects.what: Teaches Chinese and Hong Kong mahjong from scratch with a tile explorer, a hand checker that shows what you're waiting on, a solo practice table, scoring tables and a quiz.

projects.name: IB Physics Nuclear Summary
projects.title: nuclear summary
projects.why: My nuclear physics notes were spread across several booklets and I wanted one place to revise IB Physics SL Topic 7.
projects.what: Covers mass defect, binding energy and the BEN curve with three worked calculation methods, fusion and fission, and a 15-point checklist that tracks your progress.

projects.name: IB Planner
projects.title: ib planner
projects.why: My timetable, tasks and exam prep were spread across too many places, so I wanted one page that opens on today's schedule and lets me drag my to-dos into the free blocks.
projects.what: A study planner for the IB with a weekly timetable that locks in your classes, drag-and-drop to-dos, a focus queue that moves you on to the next task, exam and grade tracking, and a 14-day TMUA/TARA exam camp.

projects.name: Equilibrium
projects.title: equilibrium
projects.why: I wanted to learn game theory by building the solver behind every example, not just reading about it.
projects.what: An interactive game theory course where every game is solved live, with two of twelve chapters done so far.

projects.name: IB Definitions Lab
projects.title: ib definitions lab
projects.why: AO1 definitions are easy marks in HL Economics and Business, but only if you know the exact wording examiners want, and I kept losing them to vague phrasing. I wanted one place that drills the precise definitions and shows how the concepts connect, and then I kept going and added every Econ diagram and calculation.
projects.what: Nearly 580 AO1 definitions across HL Economics and HL Business Management. It has a dictionary, flashcards with saved progress and a concept web of how the terms link. It also has all 74 Economics diagrams that build step by step, and 35 calculations with worked examples and unlimited practice questions.
